title: Sable Aerospace partner scout notes
content:
Context:
Quick internal scratch for Sable Aerospace (mid-size avionics OEM, Seattle). Goal: test a pilot for in-cockpit assistant + maintenance triage summarization using Redwood Dedicated (data stays in their VPC). Notes are intentionally rough — meant for quick iteration and pair-check before reaching out.

Account snapshot (what I pulled together):
- HQ: Seattle, ~1.2k employees, 650 engineers across hardware/firmware/software.
- Segment: avionics and flight-control subsystems for regional jets and drones.
- CTO: Elena Morales (public interviews — pushing ML for predictive maintenance since 2023).
- Recent news: Aug 2025 teardown article about their new lightweight flight computer; announced partnership with North Harbor MRO (maintenance network) 2025-06; received $100M supplier contract Q1 2025.
- Infra posture: on AWS, VPC-first. They run sensitive telemetry pipelines; visible emphasis on SOC2 / FedRAMP readiness for some contracts.
- Pain signals: big backlog on maintenance tickets (manual reads of logs + mechanic notes), want to reduce time-to-fix and cut recurring issues by improving triage. Also interest in cockpit assistants for prompts/cheatsheets for pilots during procedures but concerned about latency/airworthiness.

Decision-makers / personas to target (mapping):
- Elena Morales — CTO (strategic buy-in, compliance risk tolerance).
- Rajesh Varma — VP Engineering (product + runtime owners).
- Priya Shah — Head of Digital Ops / Maintenance (day-to-day value owner for MRO workflows).
- Tom Hollis — Head of Safety & Compliance (regulatory gating, must be in approval chain).
- Buyer champions: likely a Sr. Systems Engineer or Product Manager within avionics SW team (internal champion recommended).

Product fit hypotheses (what to test in pilot):
1) Maintenance triage summarization: ingest mechanic notes + sensor logs -> structured incident summary + first-pass action checklist.
   - Outcomes to measure: avg time to triage, % of correct class (severity), # of follow-ups reduced.
2) In-cockpit quick reference assistant (read-only, deterministic answers + citations).
   - Outcomes: pilot acceptance tests, latency < 150ms for short queries, deterministic response trace for audit.
3) Searchable KV cache for recurring fix templates (latency and cost profile).

Suggested Redwood approach (high level):
- Private deployment (VPC) with Dedicated nodes for predictable throughput during testing.
- Data flow: Sable sends encrypted event bundles to a private ingestion endpoint; Redwood processes with preserved KV caching; outputs tagged and auditable.
- Provide a small proof-of-value (4–6 week pilot) tied to a maintenance bay group (10 mechanics).

Outbound email draft (cold -> warm sequence):
Subject: Reduce triage time for Sable's MRO teams (pilot idea)
Hi Priya,
Quick note — saw Sable's North Harbor MRO announcement and thought you might be exploring ways to reduce time spent on mechanic triage and recurring fixes. We helped a transportation OEM cut first-response triage time by ~40% with a small pilot (private inference + audit logging).
If you're open, I'd love 20 minutes to share a concrete 4-week pilot scope that keeps data in your VPC and integrates with your current ticketing exports.
Best,
Maya

Voicemail script (30s):
Hey Priya — Maya Patel from Redwood Inference. I work with teams doing private pilots for maintenance triage + cockpit knowledge assistants. Low-lift test, keeps everything in your VPC. Can I grab 20 minutes next week to show a sample triage summary?

Call framing (first meeting, 30m):
- 0–3m quick intros + goal check
- 3–8m ask: current triage flow, ticket volumes, tools (MRO, ticket exporter)
- 8–15m demo sketch: sample diagnostic logs -> triage summary (mockup) + audit trace
- 15–22m deployment/security questions (where data lives, KMS, retention)
- 22–28m success metrics and pilot scope (sample size, timeline)
- 28–30m next steps + who must be included (Tom for compliance?)

Objection handling (short bites):
- "We can't send data off-prem": Redwood Private or Dedicated in your VPC — data never leaves your network, we support KMS/HSM integration.
- "How do we trust answers (safety)?": Pilot uses deterministic prompts + citation-first design, and every response has a bounded confidence score + link to source artifact. We can enable a human-in-the-loop workflow for first 1000 queries.
- "Latency concerns for cockpit use": For cockpit queries we recommend edge prefetch + quantized model variants for sub-150ms tails; initial pilot focuses on maintenance triage (less real-time strict).
- "Regulatory sign-off": We’ll provide artifact-level audit logs, model provenance, and an attenuation checklist for cert evidence. Bring Tom early for evaluation.

Pricing/contract thinking (notes to self):
- Pilot pricing should be low-risk: 4–6 weeks, flat pilot fee $30–50k + optional engineering time. Dedicated nodes scoped (~1–2 V100 equiv for non-real-time triage).
- If they want cockpit real-time: propose reserved capacity + SLA; price migration path clearly documented.

Open questions to resolve before outreach:
- Exact ticket export format (CSV, JSON?), sample of anonymized mechanic notes (need 2 weeks worth).
- Who owns MRO tooling (vendor)? API access to ticketing? (North Harbor vs internal)
- Compliance constraints (data residency + retention) — Tom/HIPAA? likely contractual clauses for certain contracts.
- Pilot success metric thresholds (what counts as win for Priya?)

Follow-ups and immediate next actions:
- Ask Noah to see if we have any prior aerospace MRO case studies (internal GTM repo).
- Ivy: can you draft a 1-pager pilot SOW for 4-week triage pilot (target by Fri 2025-08-15)?
- Pull sample of mechanic notes from internal dataset or request anonymized sample when we get the intro.
- Schedule intro to Elena if Priya shows interest (technical + exec).

Rough timeline (if greenlit):
Week 0: scoping + access to sample exports
Week 1: ingest + mapping of fields, initial model selection + small fine-tune / prompt set
Week 2: internal validation on historical tickets + baseline measurements
Week 3: pilot live with 10 mechanics, feedback loop for corrections
Week 4: final report, playbook for rollout + next steps pricing

Notes / shorthand (random):
- Possible play: emphasize cost savings per mechanic-hour, time-to-first-action.
- Safety play: audit trail + human-in-loop reduces risk for certification.
- Internal ask: get legal to pre-draft NDA + DPA for aviation customers (Tom will want this faster).
- Keep ask to Priya tight: "20 minutes to share scope + one sample output".

Slack snippets to reuse when warming lead: 
- "Hi Priya — quick intro, Redwood helps MRO teams auto-summarize mechanic tickets. Can I share a 1-pager?"
- Follow-up: "We can run everything in your VPC and provide auditable logs for certs. 20 min?"

End of scratchpad — save this as living doc. Update after first call with Priya (capture exact objections + technical contacts).
